title: Bruised from the street (Evangelii Gaudium 49)
hook: Francis prefers a Church bruised from going out to one that's safe and closed
tomorrow: why would a pope say time is greater than space?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bakhita: her scars stayed, and knowing she was awaited changed how she lived. Hope changes life.

Cleats tell on you. Grass stains on the toes, mud dried into the studs, a scuff from somebody's heel. A pair that's never been worn is spotless, and it hasn't been anywhere. Pope Francis drew two churches like that, in Evangelii Gaudium, The Joy of the Gospel, a letter to the whole Church. One has been out on the streets all day and comes home bruised, hurting and dirty. The other stayed in, safe, holding tight to its own security, and it's grown sick from being shut up indoors. He says which one he prefers.

He says it in the first person: I prefer the bruised one. The line sits inside a call to go out and offer everyone the life of Jesus Christ. He doesn't want a Church so worried about being at the center that it gets caught in a web of obsessions and procedures. Then he names what should trouble us more than our own mistakes: brothers and sisters living without the strength, light and comfort of friendship with Jesus, with no community of faith to hold them up, and no meaning or goal in life. And he lists what he fears more than going astray. Structures that give a false sense of security. Rules that turn us into harsh judges. Habits that make us feel safe, while people are starving at the door. All the while, he writes, Jesus keeps saying, give them something to eat. Those words come from Mark's Gospel, when a hungry crowd has followed Jesus to a lonely place. So the bruise isn't the goal. It's only the mark of having gone out. A closed door keeps you clean. It also keeps everyone else outside.
screen: `I PREFER THE BRUISED ONE.` · `NOT A WEB OF PROCEDURES.` · `PEOPLE STARVING AT THE DOOR.` · `GIVE THEM SOMETHING TO EAT.` · then, large: `BRUISED, NOT CLOSED.`

segments.voice: Stand, if you can, and press your feet into the floor through your shoes. Feel where the soles are worn: every scuff is a place you went. Stay with that pressure, and let one door come to mind that you usually keep shut, a neighbor, a coworker who eats alone, a call you keep putting off.
Bruised from the street. Francis's picture of a Church that goes out and gets hurt, which he prefers to one that stays safe and closed.
Your line: bruised, not closed. The scuffs are just the record of going out. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Parishes and groups who take Evangelii Gaudium to heart speak of being a Church that goes out: visiting, feeding and welcoming people beyond their own doors.

fork.setup: your youth group can keep its cozy Friday hangout, or move it once a month to help at a crowded soup kitchen where things get messy. what would Evangelii Gaudium lean toward?

go out, even if it's messy and someone gets it wrong.
wait until the group is ready and has a perfect plan.
fork.reveal: Francis prefers a Church bruised from going out to one sick from staying in. the mess is the mark of having gone.

notes: Paraphrased from EG 49: go forth to offer everyone the life of Jesus Christ; 'I prefer a Church which is bruised, hurting and dirty because it has been out on the streets' over one unhealthy from confinement and clinging to its own security; not caught in a web of obsessions and procedures; brothers and sisters without the strength, light and consolation of friendship with Jesus, without a community of faith, without meaning and a goal; fear of structures giving false security, rules making us harsh judges, habits making us feel safe, while people starve at our door and Jesus says 'Give them something to eat' (Mk 6:37).
